title: If and then
verifiedBy: LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: NOTHING MOVES INTO THE FUTURE AFTER si. Si tu veux, si elle est libre, s'il pleut — the present stays put, and the going-to future L1-M6 taught belongs on the other side of the comma, never inside the si clause. English agrees with French here (if it rains, not if it will rain), which makes the rule cheap; what is not cheap is the apostrophe one line down.

si FUSES BEFORE il AND ils, AND BEFORE NOTHING ELSE. s'il pleut, s'ils sont libres — but si elle, si on, si tu, si Anne, all written out whole. This is the module's real trap: a learner who has met one elision applies it everywhere and writes s'elle or s'on, which no French text contains. L2-M1 already owns the fused word, inside s'il te plaît, and its note says why: s'il is si plus il.

THE CONDITIONNEL IS THE FUTUR STEM PLUS THE IMPARFAIT ENDINGS, and that is the whole of it. Take the infinitive (parler, aimer, rester), keep it entire, and add L2-M10's -ais, -ait: parlerais, aimerait, resterait. A handful of verbs have a short stem instead of the infinitive — devr-, pourr-, ser-, viendr- — and those four are worth learning as words. Nobody has to learn the endings twice.

L2-M1's je voudrais WAS THIS TENSE ALL ALONG. It shipped as a frozen politeness because it is the first conditionnel anybody needs, and now the shape underneath it is visible: voudrais, pourrais, devrais, aimerais, serait — the same ending on five stems. Nothing about je voudrais changes; it simply stops being an exception.

ONE COUNTERFACTUAL FRAME, AND THE TENSES DO NOT SWAP: si plus the imparfait, then the conditionnel. Si j'avais le temps, je viendrais. English says if I would have said it in enough dialects that the habit travels, and si je viendrais is the result — the one order French will not take. The si j'avais eu … j'aurais … version, for a thing that already did not happen, is L4-M3's and is not taught here.

ADVICE USES THE FORMS THIS MODULE JUST OPENED — tu devrais, tu pourrais, à ta place — and no new mood at all. English should, could and would are three words for what French does with one tense. L3-M3's il faut que is the impersonal alternative when you would rather not point at the person.
THE ne IS STILL WRITTEN. je ne peux pas, je ne parlerais pas — speech drops it and writing keeps it, exactly as in every module before this one.

sentences.display: Si tu veux, je peux venir demain
sentences.cue: If you want, I can come tomorrow
sentences.literal: If you want, I can to-come tomorrow

words.note: It fuses with il into s'il and with ils into s'ils, and stays whole before everything else: si elle, si tu. The same si reports a yes/no question: il a demandé si tu venais.

sentences.trap: The verb after si does not move into the future: si tu veux, never si tu voudras. English agrees, which makes this the cheap half of the module — the expensive half is one apostrophe away.
sentences.sound: see tü vuh, zhuh puh vuh-NEER duh-MAN. si is a clean ee with no y in it.

variations.display: Si tu veux, je peux rester
variations.cue: If you want, I can stay
variations.changed: a different infinitive after peux

variations.display: Si vous voulez, je peux venir demain
variations.cue: If you like, I can come tomorrow
variations.changed: vous, so veux becomes voulez

mistake.display: Si tu voudras, je peux venir demain
mistake.why: Nothing after si moves into the future: Si tu veux, je peux venir demain.

sentences.usage: Offering something without pressing it — the si half is what leaves the other person the choice.

sentences.display: S'il pleut, je reste à la maison
sentences.cue: If it rains, I'm staying home
sentences.literal: If-it rains, I stay at the house

words.note: The present beside L2-M10's pleuvait, and the il in front of it stands for nobody — the same empty il as il y a and il faut.
The present of L1-M6's rester. One French present covers both English ones: je reste is I stay and I am staying alike.

sentences.trap: s' before il and ils, and before nothing else. s'il, s'ils — then si elle, si on, si Anne, si tu, all whole. A learner who has learnt one elision applies it everywhere and writes s'elle, which no French text contains.
sentences.sound: seel pluh, zhuh rest a la meh-ZON. s'il is one syllable, and pleut ends in a pursed uh.

variations.display: S'ils sont libres, je reste ici
variations.cue: If they're free, I'm staying here
variations.changed: ils, so si fuses again — s'ils

variations.display: Si elle vient, je reste à la maison
variations.cue: If she comes, I'm staying home
variations.changed: elle, so si stays whole

mistake.display: Si il pleut, je reste à la maison
mistake.why: si and il fuse into one written word: S'il pleut, je reste à la maison.

sentences.usage: The everyday weather condition, and the sentence where the fusion cannot be avoided.
sentences.mnemonic: s' only ever meets an i.

sentences.display: Si elle est libre, elle vient avec nous
sentences.cue: If she's free, she's coming with us
sentences.literal: If she is free, she comes with us

words.note: The present of L1-M10's venir. The plural doubles the n and sounds it: elle vient is nasal, elles viennent is not.

sentences.trap: si elle, never s'elle. The fusion reaches il and ils and stops — elle, on, tu and every name keep their si whole, however awkward the two vowels look side by side.
sentences.sound: see el eh LEEBR, el vyan a-vek NOO. vient is one nasal syllable, vyan.

variations.display: Si elle est libre, elle vient avec moi
variations.cue: If she's free, she's coming with me
variations.changed: moi rather than nous

variations.display: S'il est libre, il vient avec nous
variations.cue: If he's free, he's coming with us
variations.changed: il, so si fuses

mistake.display: S'elle est libre, elle vient avec nous
mistake.why: Only il and ils take the fusion: Si elle est libre, elle vient avec nous.

sentences.usage: Making a plan that hangs on somebody else being free.

sentences.display: Tu devrais parler à ton patron
sentences.cue: You should talk to your boss
sentences.literal: You would-must to-talk to your boss

words.note: L3-M2's dois in the conditionnel, on the short stem devr-. The infinitive after it still stands bare: tu devrais parler, never devrais de parler.

sentences.trap: There is no French word for should. French bends dois instead, and English's should, could and would all turn out to be one French tense wearing three English hats.
sentences.sound: tü duh-VREH par-LAY a ton pa-TRON. The -ais ending is an open eh.

variations.display: Tu devrais rentrer tôt
variations.cue: You should go home early
variations.changed: a different infinitive after it

variations.display: Il devrait parler à son patron
variations.cue: He should talk to his boss
variations.changed: il, so the ending loses its s and nothing else moves

mistake.display: Tu devrais de parler à ton patron
mistake.why: Nothing goes between the conditionnel and its infinitive: Tu devrais parler à ton patron.

sentences.usage: Advice with the edge taken off — tu dois orders, tu devrais suggests.
sentences.mnemonic: should is dois with an -ais on it.

sentences.display: Tu pourrais m'aider, s'il te plaît ?
sentences.literal: You would-can to-help-me, if-it you pleases?

words.note: L2-M1's peux in the conditionnel, on the stem pourr-. tu peux asks whether you can; tu pourrais asks whether you would.

sentences.trap: The two r's are the stem and not a spelling slip: peux becomes pourr-, exactly as dois becomes devr-. Both are written double and said as one r, so only the page ever tells you.
sentences.sound: tü poo-REH meh-DAY, seel tuh PLEH.

variations.display: Tu pourrais rester ici ?
variations.cue: Could you stay here?
variations.changed: a different infinitive after it

variations.display: Il pourrait m'aider
variations.cue: He could help me
variations.changed: il, so the ending loses its s

mistake.display: Tu pourais m'aider, s'il te plaît ?
mistake.why: The stem carries two r's: Tu pourrais m'aider, s'il te plaît ?

sentences.usage: Asking a favour of somebody you tutoie, one step politer than tu peux.

sentences.display: À ta place, je parlerais au patron
sentences.cue: If I were you, I'd talk to the boss
sentences.literal: At your place, I would-talk to-the boss

words.note: Three frozen words doing the job of English's if I were you, and they need no verb at all. The conditionnel then carries the advice in the second half.
L2-M7's parler with the whole infinitive kept and -ais added. Every regular -er verb builds its conditionnel this way, so one example is the rule.

sentences.trap: This is where the economy is visible on the page: the ending is L2-M10's imparfait, bolted onto the infinitive. Learn one set of endings and the conditionnel of every regular verb comes free.
sentences.sound: a ta plas, zhuh par-luh-REH o pa-TRON. The e in the middle of parlerais is barely there.

variations.display: À ta place, je ne parlerais pas
variations.cue: If I were you, I wouldn't say anything
variations.changed: the advice reversed, with ne and pas round the conditionnel

variations.display: Il parlerait au patron
variations.cue: He would talk to the boss
variations.changed: il, so the ending loses its s

mistake.display: À ma place, je parlerais au patron
mistake.why: The place is the one you are advising, not your own: À ta place, je parlerais au patron.

sentences.usage: Advice given by standing in the other person's shoes — the frame French uses where English says if I were you.

sentences.display: Si j'avais le temps, je viendrais avec toi
sentences.cue: If I had time, I'd come with you
sentences.literal: If I-had the time, I would-come with you

words.note: L2-M10's avais with je elided onto it and written as one word, the same fusion as j'ai and j'étais. The imparfait is what si takes whenever a conditionnel follows.
L1-M10's venir in the conditionnel, on the short stem viendr- rather than the infinitive. The ending is the same -ais as everywhere else.

sentences.trap: The conditionnel goes in the SECOND half only. Si je viendrais is the English if I would showing through the French, and it is the one order the language will not take: si takes the imparfait and the wish sits after the comma.
sentences.sound: see zha-VEH luh TAHN, zhuh vyan-DREH a-vek TWA.

variations.display: Si j'avais le temps, je viendrais avec vous
variations.cue: If I had time, I'd come with you
variations.changed: vous, for somebody you do not tutoie

variations.display: S'il avait le temps, il viendrait avec toi
variations.cue: If he had time, he'd come with you
variations.changed: il, so si fuses and both verbs lose their s

mistake.display: Si je viendrais, je serais content
mistake.why: si never takes a conditionnel: Si j'avais le temps, je viendrais avec toi.

sentences.usage: The wish that says no — a refusal with its reason folded into the first half.
sentences.mnemonic: si takes the imparfait; the wish takes the conditionnel.

sentences.display: Ce serait super, mais je ne peux pas
sentences.cue: That would be great, but I can't
sentences.literal: It would-be great, but I not can not

words.note: The conditionnel of est, on the stem ser-. ce serait is French's that would be, and it is the commonest polite reply the language has.

sentences.trap: ce serait, not il serait. The empty ce is what points at a whole situation, exactly as it does in c'est vrai — il would have to stand for some particular thing.
sentences.sound: suh suh-REH sü-PEHR, meh zhuh nuh puh PA.

variations.display: Ce serait bien
variations.cue: That would be nice
variations.changed: shorter, and warmer than super

variations.display: Ce serait super, mais il faut que j'aille au travail
variations.cue: That would be great, but I have to go to work
variations.changed: L3-M3's obligation supplying the reason

mistake.display: Ce sera super, mais je ne peux pas
mistake.why: The regret needs the conditionnel: Ce serait super, mais je ne peux pas.

sentences.usage: Turning something down warmly — the conditionnel is what makes it sound like a regret rather than a refusal.

sentences.display: Si tu voulais, tu pourrais venir avec nous
sentences.cue: If you wanted to, you could come with us
sentences.literal: If you wanted, you would-can to-come with us

words.note: L1-M3's veux in the imparfait — L2-M10's ending on the voul- stem. This is the shape si takes whenever a conditionnel follows it.

sentences.trap: The pair is fixed and does not swap: imparfait on the si side, conditionnel on the other. si tu voudrais puts both wishes on the same side and is the commonest error English produces here.
sentences.sound: see tü voo-LEH, tü poo-REH vuh-NEER a-vek NOO.

variations.display: Si tu voulais, tu pourrais rester ici
variations.cue: If you wanted to, you could stay here
variations.changed: a different infinitive in the second half

variations.display: S'il voulait, il pourrait venir avec nous
variations.cue: If he wanted to, he could come with us
variations.changed: il, so si fuses and both verbs lose their s

mistake.display: Si tu voudrais, tu pourrais venir avec nous
mistake.why: si takes the imparfait: Si tu voulais, tu pourrais venir avec nous.

sentences.usage: An invitation left entirely open, which is the politest one French has.

sentences.display: J'aimerais venir, mais il faut que j'aille au travail
sentences.cue: I'd love to come, but I have to go to work
sentences.literal: I-would-like to-come, but it is-necessary that I-go to-the work

words.note: L1-M1's aime built the regular way — the whole infinitive aimer plus -ais. It is the warmer neighbour of L2-M1's je voudrais, which is the same tense.

sentences.trap: L2-M1 shipped je voudrais frozen, as a politeness with no explanation. This is the explanation: it is the conditionnel of veux, and j'aimerais, je pourrais and je devrais are its neighbours rather than new words.
sentences.sound: zheh-muh-REH vuh-NEER, meh eel fo kuh ZHY o tra-VYE.

variations.display: Je voudrais venir, mais il faut que j'aille au travail
variations.cue: I'd like to come, but I have to go to work
variations.changed: je voudrais, which L2-M1 shipped frozen and which is this same tense

variations.display: J'aimerais venir avec vous
variations.cue: I'd love to come with you
variations.changed: the wish on its own, with no obligation against it

mistake.display: J'aime venir, mais il faut que j'aille au travail
mistake.why: j'aime states a habit; the wish needs the conditionnel: J'aimerais venir.

sentences.usage: Declining an invitation you would actually have accepted, which is what the conditionnel is for.
sentences.mnemonic: voudrais and aimerais are the same tense.
